question: Why is monotherapy strictly avoided in the pharmacological management of tuberculosis?

options.A: It causes immediate and severe renal failure.
options.B: It invariably leads to treatment failure and the rapid emergence of drug-resistant strains.
options.C: It is too expensive for routine clinical practice in Nigeria.
options.D: It accelerates the replication rate of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

explanation: Because Mycobacterium tuberculosis naturally contains spontaneous chromosomal mutations for resistance, using a single drug allows resistant mutants to survive and multiply, leading to treatment failure. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h1)

question: What is the primary pharmacological justification for combining multiple anti-tuberculosis drugs in a regimen?

options.A: To target different metabolic pathways and eradicate both active and dormant bacilli
options.B: To shorten the total duration of treatment to less than one week
options.C: To eliminate the need for patient monitoring and follow-up sputum tests
options.D: To prevent all known adverse drug reactions from occurring

explanation: Combination therapy utilizes drugs with different mechanisms to effectively eliminate actively replicating bacilli as well as dormant persister organisms. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which first-line anti-tuberculosis drug acts primarily by inhibiting the synthesis of mycolic acids in the mycobacterial cell wall?
explanation: Isoniazid is a potent bactericidal agent specifically known for inhibiting mycolic acid synthesis, thereby disrupting the cell wall of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary mechanism of action of rifampicin against Mycobacterium tuberculosis?

options.A: Inhibition of DNA-dependent RNA synthesis by binding to RNA polymerase
options.B: Disruption of bacterial membrane potential in acidic environments
options.C: Inhibition of arabinosyl transferases to block cell wall formation
options.D: Chelation of essential metal ions within the bacterial cytoplasm

explanation: Rifampicin binds to the beta-subunit of bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, directly inhibiting RNA synthesis and bacterial transcription. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h2)

question: When are second-line anti-tuberculosis agents typically indicated for clinical use?

options.A: During the standard two-week initial phase for all newly diagnosed patients
options.B: When patients have drug resistance, intolerance, or contraindications to first-line drugs
options.C: As a prophylactic measure for healthcare workers exposed to latent TB
options.D: To completely replace the need for Directly Observed Therapy

explanation: Second-line agents are reserved for cases involving drug-resistant strains, severe toxicity, or when first-line drugs cannot be safely used. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which of the following represents a novel mechanism of action introduced by newer second-line drugs like bedaquiline?
explanation: Bedaquiline works through a novel mechanism by inhibiting mycobacterial ATP synthase, which disrupts energy generation in the bacterium. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which anti-tuberculosis drug is uniquely effective against semi-dormant intracellular bacilli located in acidic environments?
explanation: Pyrazinamide works exceptionally well in the acidic environments found within macrophages and caseous cavities, targeting semi-dormant bacilli. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why are multiple drugs required to target the different metabolic pools of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in the body?

options.A: Because different bacillary populations reside in distinct tissue niches and exhibit varying metabolic rates
options.B: Because single drugs neutralize each other when mixed in the bloodstream
options.C: Because bacterial populations in the lungs are completely immune to bactericidal agents
options.D: Because the human immune system destroys rapidly dividing bacteria without drug assistance

explanation: M. tuberculosis populations exist in different pools (rapidly dividing, semi-dormant, and dormant), requiring drugs with specific activities tailored to those environments. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary objective of the intensive phase of standard tuberculosis treatment?

options.A: To eliminate persistent dormant bacilli in caseous tissue over a four-month period
options.B: To rapidly reduce the massive bacillary load and prevent secondary drug resistance
options.C: To test the patient for potential drug allergies using monotherapy
options.D: To replace the need for patient follow-up sputum examinations

explanation: The intensive phase utilizes a four-drug regimen for two months to quickly lower the bacterial load and stop drug resistance from emerging. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is the core practice involved in Directly Observed Therapy (DOTS)?

options.A: Patients are given a six-month supply of drugs to take independently at home.
options.B: A trained healthcare worker or volunteer watches the patient swallow every dose of medication.
options.C: Intravenous infusions are administered exclusively in hospital intensive care units.
options.D: Sputum cultures are evaluated daily without patient interaction.

explanation: DOTS requires a healthcare worker or designated observer to physically watch the patient swallow each dose to ensure absolute adherence. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which supplement is commonly co-administered with isoniazid to prevent peripheral neuropathy?
explanation: Pyridoxine (vitamin B6) is routinely given alongside isoniazid to prevent or treat drug-induced peripheral neuropathy. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h6)

question: A patient taking ethambutol reports difficulty reading and trouble distinguishing between red and green colors. What adverse effect should the nurse suspect?
explanation: Ethambutol is known to cause optic neuritis, which manifests as decreased visual acuity and impaired red-green color discrimination. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h6)

question: How is multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) formally defined?

options.A: Resistance to ethambutol and pyrazinamide only
options.B: Resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin
options.C: Resistance to all available first-line and second-line injectable drugs
options.D: Resistance to any single fluoroquinolone medication

explanation: MDR-TB is specifically defined as resistance to at least the two core first-line drugs: isoniazid and rifampicin. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h7)

question: Which of the following criteria distinguishes extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB) from MDR-TB?

options.A: Additional resistance to a fluoroquinolone and at least one second-line injectable agent
options.B: Complete clearance of the bacteria from sputum within two weeks
options.C: Resistance limited exclusively to pyrazinamide and ethambutol
options.D: Total absence of any hepatotoxic side effects during treatment

explanation: XDR-TB requires MDR-TB criteria plus additional resistance to any fluoroquinolone and at least one second-line injectable drug. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h7)

question: A patient starting rifampicin calls the clinic distressed because their urine and tears have turned a reddish-orange color. What is the most appropriate nursing response?

options.A: Instruct the patient to stop taking the medication immediately and report to the emergency room.
options.B: Explain that this is a harmless, expected side effect of rifampicin and reassure the patient.
options.C: Acknowledge that this indicates severe liver failure and arrange for immediate hospitalization.
options.D: Advise the patient to double their fluid intake to flush the toxic dye out of their kidneys.

explanation: Rifampicin causes a harmless reddish-orange discoloration of body fluids, and reassuring the patient prevents unnecessary treatment discontinuation. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h8)

question: Which of the following home care instructions should a nurse provide to a newly diagnosed pulmonary TB patient to protect household contacts?

options.A: Isolate all family members in separate houses for the duration of the six-month therapy.
options.B: Ensure good indoor ventilation, practice proper coughing etiquette, and minimize close contact until non-infectious.
options.C: Burn all personal clothing and eating utensils used by the patient daily.
options.D: Wear surgical masks continuously while sleeping alone in a locked room.

explanation: Promoting good room ventilation and proper cough hygiene effectively reduces airborne transmission risks to family members at home. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h8)
